The constitutional system selects national leadership through elections and divides legislative, executive and judicial authority. The 2026 election calendar, current party-qualification rules, September opposition spending inquiry, and February and June Supreme Court rulings provide dated implementation evidence. These support electoral and judicial constraints without assuming that formal checks always function effectively. State-level referendum and recall mechanisms are assessed separately from federal arrangements.
Focused six-question reassessment: Independent technical institutions and executive action operate under constitutional law and congressional checks. Federal citizen law initiatives are absent; defined constitutional succession is narrower than free party replacement, and fixed elected terms constrain postponement.
